You will join the Equities Live Risk, PnL and TradeFeeds team, working with grid computing and messaging technologies to deliver business-critical data across a globally distributed organization spanning Europe and India. This role places you at the center of Citi's trading technology, solving complex problems in high-volume, low-latency financial systems. Responsibilities Design and build scalable .NET applications that power real-time risk generation and PnL reporting for equities trading. Write comprehensive unit tests using frameworks such as NUnit, xUnit, or Shouldly to maintain code quality and reliability. Conduct performance testing and profiling to keep applications robust and scalable under high-volume financial data processing. Troubleshoot, diagnose, and resolve code issues and performance bottlenecks across live trading systems. Apply design patterns and system architecture principles to solve complex technical problems within a distributed messaging environment. Identify and define system enhancements by analyzing and interpreting existing application code. Collaborate with a globally distributed development team across Europe and India with minimal supervision. Act as a subject matter expert, guiding senior stakeholders and team members through technical decisions. Required Qualifications & Skills Hold a bachelor's degree in computer science, information technology, engineering, or a related field. Bring 5 to 9 years of developer experience delivering large and complex software projects. Apply strong C# skills across both .NET Framework 4.5.2+ and .NET 5+ environments. Write comprehensive unit tests using frameworks such as NUnit, xUnit, or Shouldly. Analyze and optimize .NET application performance to support high-volume, low-latency systems. Use version control and CI/CD tools such as Git and GitLab or GitHub to manage code delivery. Beneficial Skills & Qualifications Experience or familiarity with high-volume, low-latency, highly available financial systems, trading platforms, or financial data processing. Exposure to additional programming languages such as Python, Java, or Bash, and operating systems such as Linux. Understanding of one or more messaging technologies such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, or Solace. Clear understanding of design patterns and how to apply them to solve complex technical problems.
